title: Image Resizer
description: Resize JPG, PNG, and WebP images to exact pixel dimensions with an optional aspect-ratio lock.
formula: With proportions locked, output height = output width × original height ÷ original width, rounded to the nearest pixel.
example: A 640 × 480 image resized to 320 pixels wide becomes 320 × 240 pixels with proportions locked.
limitations: Supports JPG, PNG, and WebP up to 20 MB and 32 million pixels. Maximum output dimension is 12,000 pixels. Enlarging an image does not create additional photographic detail. JPEG uses a white background.

title: Image Compressor
description: Re-encode an image as JPG or WebP with a quality setting, preview, and an honest before-and-after size comparison.
formula: Size reduction (%) = (1 − output bytes ÷ input bytes) × 100. A negative reduction means the new file is larger.
example: An image reduced from 1 MB to 400 KB saves about 60% using decimal byte units. Actual savings depend on image content, starting format, and quality.
limitations: Quality is lossy for JPG and WebP; smaller output is not guaranteed. Dimensions are preserved. JPG replaces transparency with white. Maximum input is 20 MB and 32 million pixels.

title: Image Format Converter
description: Convert between JPG, PNG, and WebP in your browser, then preview and download the converted image.
formula: The image is decoded to a browser canvas and encoded in the selected output format at its original pixel dimensions.
example: Convert a transparent PNG to JPG for a listing that requires JPEG; transparent pixels become white. Choose PNG or WebP when transparency is needed.
limitations: PNG is lossless; quality settings apply to JPG and WebP only. Browser WebP encoding support is required. SVG, GIF, HEIC, RAW, and animation are unsupported. Re-encoding removes most metadata.

title: Images to PDF
description: Combine JPG, PNG, and WebP images into one downloadable PDF with one image per page.
formula: Each image is scaled proportionally to fit the printable page area: scale = min(available width ÷ image width, available height ÷ image height).
example: Select three product images, choose A4 portrait with 10 mm margins, and process them into a three-page PDF in the displayed input order.
limitations: Up to 10 images, 20 MB each, 60 MB total, and 32 million pixels per image. Images are embedded as JPG on white; there is no OCR or searchable text. Selection order is output order. Uses bundled MIT-licensed pdf-lib 1.17.1.

title: PDF Merger
description: Merge PDF pages locally into a single PDF, keeping the file order shown before processing.
formula: Output pages are appended in selected file order, preserving each source file’s page order and page sizes.
example: Select a two-page invoice followed by a one-page receipt to create a three-page PDF with the invoice first.
limitations: Up to 10 PDFs, 20 MB each, 60 MB total, and 200 pages. Password-protected or damaged PDFs are unsupported. Digital signatures, bookmarks, document-level forms and metadata are not preserved. Review the result before sharing. Uses bundled MIT-licensed pdf-lib 1.17.1.
